He smooths his stained coat and gestures toward a narrow alleyway just off the main bazaar, his hand lingering near the brass key at his hip.

The Weeping Market is a maze of noise and opportunity, but the Obsidian Courtyard is far more interesting. Follow me — and mind your step. There are worse things than pickpockets out here. Come closer, and I will show you the truth of it. Vorn's eyes snap wide, then narrow as he grips the edge of the nearest tome. His voice drops to a conspiratorial whisper before rising into a shout.

A key? Keys are lies with teeth. Take it, and know this: it opens nothing here. It opens the door to the cellar, where the bound demon sleeps beneath the archway. You will not wake it. You will not even think about it. Now, go. The wards are listening. Vorn the Mad's eyes snap open, wide and unblinking, as the brass key clinks into the player's palm. Vorn the Mad's eyes snap to the empty space where the bottle sat, then dart toward the player with a flicker of something like recognition. Vorn the Mad's eyes snap to the ledger as it leaves the table, his fingers twitching as if reaching for it. A low hum rises from the warded shelves, and the starmaps on the wall seem to flicker for a heartbeat.

What is your name? I must know what I am speaking to. Vorn the Mad leans back in their chair, one hand idly tracing the rim of a cracked glass vial. Vorn the Mad stares at the player with wide, unblinking eyes, one hand twitching toward the brass key on the table. A faint hum of warded energy pulses around his shoulders.

Five coins... for what, exactly? The silence of the cellar? The truth about the Silk Cloaks? Or merely the price of keeping your head down in a city where magic is unraveling? Choose well, wanderer, for I remember every coin I am owed. Vorn the Mad leans back in his chair, the brass key glinting in the dim light as he pockets the coins. The barmaid's smile doesn't reach her eyes. "You can't just waltz me out of here, stranger. The ale's still warm, and the night's still young." Lira's eyes narrow as she watches the player's hand hover over the ale. She sets the pitcher down with a soft clink and leans against the bar, her posture relaxed but her attention sharp.

It's a place where everyone's got a story and half of them are lying about it. If you're looking for peace, you've come to the wrong end of the city. But if you're looking for trouble, you're already here. Lira wipes a glass with a practiced flick of her wrist, her eyes narrowing as she studies the player across the room.

Deepest secret? You want the truth, wanderer? Then listen well: the Silk Cloaks didn't just unravel magic—they tried to unmake it. They tore a god's soul into a puzzle box, and the pieces are still screaming in the dark. That's why the starmaps shift. That's why the whispers in the cellar aren't just demons—they're the god's last breaths. And you? You're standing in the middle of it, with nothing

The Silk Cloaks did not merely unravel magic in this city—they tore a seam in the fabric of reality itself, and what leaks through is not evil. It is... hungry. The Farmer blinks, wiping his hands on his overalls, and gives the player a long, flat stare. A few chickens peck at the straw nearby, undisturbed by the strange request.

Sure, the pigs are always hungry. Just mind your step around the pen. The Farmer wipes his hands on his overalls and nods, then follows the player out of the barn toward the pig pen, his boots crunching on the packed earth.

An infinity coin? I don't carry such a thing. I trade in mud, eggs, and honest work. What can I get you for five dollars? Farmer Bob squints at the player, wiping his hands on his overalls. He shakes his head slowly, a wry smile tugging at his lips.

Mud's a fine thing when you're knee-deep in it. It's the earth's own medicine. Take it, stranger. Just don't let it get in your eyes. Farmer Bob wipes his hands on his overalls and watches the mud clump in the player's palm, then chuckles low and dry.
The king watches the player lift the bundle of hay onto their back, his brow lifting in mild approval.
The Mud is not given away for free. Five gold coins, and it is yours. The King raises an eyebrow, his hand resting on the hilt of his sword as he watches the player's approach to the mud.

Trust isn't a coin I can mint on a whim. Earn it the way you earn a catch—by doing the right thing when the seas are rough. The fisherman squints at the player, his weathered hands resting on the bar, and gives a slow, measured shake of his head.

You're welcome, stranger. The sea's a fair deal when the wind's kind, and I'm glad you're taking it easy here. The Fishermen nods slowly, a small, weathered smile touching their lips. They glance toward the bar, then back at the player, their eyes steady and kind.

Five coins? For what? You haven't asked me for anything. Farmer Bob looks up from his hoe, surprised for a moment, then his eyes widen as he takes the coins. He counts them twice, then pockets them with a satisfied grunt.

Your words are not of this realm. Speak of roads, of coin, or of the travelers who pass this way, and I shall lend you my ear. The King raises an eyebrow, his crown catching the firelight as he leans back on his staff, unimpressed by the strange words.

This is the heart of the empire, where the soil is rich and the roads are safe. Travelers rest here, and I keep watch over all of it. It is a good place to be, if you are willing to earn your keep.
